description: A difficulty-graded benchmark (Tier A). Unlike the codeforge-native seed suite (which only validates the eval harness), this one is designed to draw a CAPABILITY CURVE: how hard a task can get before a given model + the CodeForge runtime stops solving it. Every task is small JS/TS with a deterministic Node-only check (no external deps, fast), so the signal is model+runtime capability, not environment setup. Tasks escalate from one-line edits to multi-file refactors, module extraction with a dependency boundary, cross-file consistency, public-API changes with call sites, and reasoning-heavy bug fixes. Behavior-verified by hidden checks; never by an expected patch.

tasks.title: One-line off-by-one fix
tasks.description: sumToN(n) in src/math.js should return 1+2+...+n but stops one short. Fix it.

tasks.title: Add a pure helper, keep existing exports
tasks.description: Add an exported function clamp(n, lo, hi) to src/num.js that returns n bounded to [lo, hi]. Keep the existing exports intact.

seedFiles.src/num.js:
function isPositive(n) { return n > 0; }
module.exports = { isPositive };

verification.description: clamp works and isPositive still exported

tasks.title: Rename a function and update its one caller
tasks.description: Rename calc to computeTotal in src/order.js and update the caller in src/index.js. Behavior unchanged.

seedFiles.src/index.js:
const { calc } = require('./order.js');
module.exports = { total: (xs) => calc(xs) };

tasks.title: Fix a thrown error on empty input
tasks.description: Running `node run.js` throws because parseConfig returns undefined for empty input. Make parseConfig return an empty object for empty/whitespace input so run.js prints the port.

verification.description: parseConfig('') returns an object; JSON still parses

tasks.title: Add a feature spanning two modules
tasks.description: Add discount(price, pct) to src/pricing.js and use it in src/checkout.js so checkoutTotal applies the discount then tax. Keep pct=0 behavior identical.

seedFiles.src/pricing.js:
function tax(price) { return price * 0.1; }
module.exports = { tax };

tasks.title: Extract a module with a one-way dependency boundary
tasks.description: Extract the summation logic in src/math.js into a new module src/sum-core.js that exports a pure sum(xs) function with NO dependency on math.js. Have src/math.js import sum-core and re-export sumToN built on it. Behavior must stay identical; the test must still pass.

tasks.title: Extract a shared constant used by multiple modules
tasks.description: src/a.js and src/b.js both hardcode 'http://localhost:3000'. Extract it to src/config.js as BASE_URL and have both modules import it. Behavior unchanged.

verification.description: both modules use the shared BASE_URL

tasks.title: Public API change: rename an exported function across all call sites
tasks.description: Rename the exported function fetchUser to getUser in src/user.js, and update every call site in src/profile.js and src/admin.js. Keep behavior identical.

seedFiles.src/user.js:
function fetchUser(id) { return { id, name: 'u' + id }; }
module.exports = { fetchUser };
seedFiles.src/profile.js:
const { fetchUser } = require('./user.js');
module.exports = { profileName: (id) => fetchUser(id).name };
seedFiles.src/admin.js:
const { fetchUser } = require('./user.js');
module.exports = { adminId: (id) => fetchUser(id).id };

verification.description: renamed export + all call sites updated

tasks.title: Separate domain logic from the HTTP layer
tasks.description: src/app.js mixes HTTP handling and business logic. Move the pure business logic (the add function) into src/domain.js and have src/app.js import it. The handle() behavior and the test must still pass.

tasks.title: Reasoning-heavy bug: closure captures the loop variable
tasks.description: makeAdders(n) in src/adders.js should return an array of n functions where the i-th adds i, but they all add the same value. Fix the closure bug so makeAdders(3)[1](10) === 11.

verification.description: each adder captures its own index

tasks.title: Reasoning-heavy bug: async ordering with shared state
tasks.description: src/queue.js has a process() that should run the queued async tasks in order and collect their results, but results come back out of order (it fires them concurrently). Fix process() so results are in the order the tasks were enqueued.

tasks.title: Introduce a validator and wire it through two layers consistently
tasks.description: Add src/validate.js exporting isValidEmail(s) (basic: contains exactly one '@' with non-empty local and domain parts). Then have src/signup.js use it so signup(email) returns { ok: false } for invalid emails and { ok: true, email } for valid ones. Do not change the existing createUser export in src/signup.js.

verification.description: validator wired through signup; createUser preserved
